neighbours.label: The word just before a money/funds noun in public-finance text (raise [money], appropriate [money], amount of [funding], urgently needed [funds])
fire: The school held a bake sale to raise money for new computers.
Congress voted to appropriate money for flood relief.
The city received the largest amount of federal grants in the state.
Hospitals warned that urgently needed funds had not arrived.
Volunteers ran a marathon to raise funds for the shelter.
The council failed to allocate money for road repairs.
The bill would release billions of dollars in aid to farmers.
Donors pledged a record amount of funding for cancer research.
quiet: The school held a bake sale on the last Friday of term.
Congress voted to rename the post office in the town.
The city received the largest number of visitors in the state.
Hospitals warned that the flu season had arrived early.
Volunteers ran a marathon through the old town center.
The council failed to agree on the new parking rules.
The bill would change the rules for farm inspections.
Donors attended a dinner at the cancer research center.

predictions: Verbs and frames that set up money/funds in finance or budget text reach 0.4-0.7; the same frames in non-financial text stay under 0.2.
notes: Probe: 'largest amount of' 0.701 (same for 'amount of rain', so 'amount of' fires on its own); 'lottery to raise' 0.466 vs 'meeting to raise awareness' 0.193; 'refused to appropriate' 0.425; 'urgently needed' 0.419 (same before 'trucks'); 'charity spent' 0.058. A next-token predictor of funds; near misses removing the finance setup are uncertain.
